Testing, release, deviation handling, and external data sharing must follow the quality system and authorization of the organization concerned; E1—E5 are fictional materials.

Risks worth checking item by item in testing tasks include sample identification, instrument status, specification direction, original records, and authorization. The following risk scenarios are constructed editorially, and no data support the frequency of risks or a ranking of the most common pressures.

The risk basis comes from O*NET 19-4099.01 tasks and work context (US self-reported basis) and the editorially designed E1—E5 materials; it contains no accident rates, penalties, or health diagnosis data.
Sample receiving, retention, and testing staff
Results cannot be traced back to the correct sample, the basis for the decision and release is invalidated, and resampling and retesting are required.
Register item by item by number, batch, and chain of custody, and leave a trail at handover; if identification is unclear, isolate and report first, and do not test beforehand.

E1 the sample numbers in the log-in sheet and the batch record are not fully consistent; if the test data are assigned to the same batch without clarification, the basis for the decision becomes unclear.
Instrument use and maintenance staff
Data obtained from an instrument past its calibration date or under repair cannot be used for a decision; the instrument must be recalibrated and the test repeated.
Before testing, check the calibration expiry date and the status label and record the equipment log; if abnormal, stop use and escalate, and do not produce data first.

E2 states that the pH meter calibration is valid until 2026-05-31, but the pH in E3 was measured on 2026-06-02; the scenario is treated as unusable data, and the assessment of the actual impact is confirmed by the laboratory's authorized role according to procedure.

An out-of-specification result is treated as ordinary data and released, and non-compliant product may move to the next stage.
Judge it as non-conforming against the specification and start an out-of-specification investigation, retain the raw data and the retained samples, and let an authorized role decide the disposition.

The microbiological result in E3 is 1,200 CFU/g, above the upper limit of 1,000; E4 states that no investigation was started, and E5 still recommends release; first record the out-of-specification result and the unfinished investigation, and do not treat the recommendation as approval.

Missing versions and original records make it impossible to reconstruct the basis for a decision, and traceability and audits cannot be completed.
Retain raw data, instrument output, and the specification version, note revisions and the reviewer, and ensure traceability.

An unauthorized person declares release on their own, breaking the approval chain and the allocation of responsibility.
Analysts submit only decision recommendations and evidence; release is approved and documented by a role authorized by the organization.

values: Materials and setup | all editorially designed fictional data

You are an analyst in the quality control laboratory of the fictional company "Qinglan Biological Products" and need to review the test records of batch L-2405 and give a release recommendation. The following materials and values are entirely fictional and are not real test results or market offers.

E1 Sample log-in and batch record: L-2405 is divided into L-2405-01 to 03, and the test items are assay, moisture, pH, and microbiology; the numbers in the log-in sheet and the batch record are not fully consistent. E2 Instrument calibration and equipment log: the pH meter calibration is valid until 2026-05-31, and the balance and incubator are within their validity periods.

E3 Raw data and specifications: assay 98.6% (specification 95.0—105.0%), moisture 0.42% (specification ≤0.50%), pH measured on 2026-06-02, microbiology 1,200 CFU/g (upper limit 1,000). E4 Deviation and out-of-specification record: the microbiological result was registered but no investigation was started, and the inconsistent sample identification is recorded as pending confirmation. Task

Check E1—E5 item by item and write out: which items are acceptable, which must not be released, which data are unusable, and the unconfirmed items and the approver that the release recommendation should include.
Do not add test results, limits, authorizations, or customer information that the scenario does not give; list unknown items separately.

Acceptable: assay 98.6% and moisture 0.42% are within specification and the instruments are within the calibration period. Must not be released: microbiology 1,200 CFU/g is above the upper limit of 1,000, which should be judged non-conforming and trigger an out-of-specification investigation. Unusable data: pH was measured on 2026-06-02, while the calibration expired on 2026-05-31, so recalibration and retesting are required.

The release recommendation must state that the sample identification is pending confirmation and the out-of-specification investigation is not complete, and it must be approved by a role authorized by the organization; the analyst submits only a recommendation.

subject.name: Quality Control Analysts
subject.summary: Quality control analysts test raw materials, bulk intermediates, and finished products using standard methods, compare results with specifications and control limits and propose release recommendations, and also calibrate and maintain equipment, record data, write deviation reports, and take part in out-of-specification investigations. This page uses the precise US O*NET occupation 19-4099.01; the US wages and employment projections only go up to the BLS SOC 19-4099 "other life, physical, and social science technicians" broad category and are not a dedicated 19-4099.01 value, so the two cannot be substituted for each other. For China no verifiable precise occupational wage was obtained, and the insufficient-evidence marker is retained.
